<ticket source="">
# # Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

- Ticket: request
- State: open

## Description

# Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

**Type:** bug / error message

`POST /api/tasks` with `{}` answers `500` and `{"error": "Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 1."}`. With `{"title": ""}` it creates an empty task. A body that is not JSON also answers a 500 with the parser's message. On the page, adding an empty task does nothing visible.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `POST /api/tasks` with a missing, empty or blank (only spaces) `title`, or a `title` that is not a string, answers `400` with `{"error": "title is required"}`, and no task is created.
2. The same rule applies to `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` when the body has a `title`.
3. A title longer than 200 characters (after trimming) answers `400` with `{"error": "title must be at most 200 characters"}`. Titles are saved trimmed.
4. A request body that is not valid JSON answers `400` with `{"error": "invalid JSON body"}`.
5. An unexpected error answers `500` with `{"error": "internal error"}` and never shows the internal message to the client (log it on the server instead).
6. When adding a task fails, the page shows the error message from the API.
7. Tests cover these cases.
</ticket>

plan.summary:
Small bug fix, one task. Today `POST /api/tasks` hands `body.title` straight to SQLite. A missing or non-string title gives a 500 with a SQLite message, and an empty title creates an empty task. `PATCH` has no title check either. `readJson` throws on bad JSON, and the catch in `createServer` (`src/app.ts`) returns `err.message` with a 500, which leaks internals. On the page, the submit handler in `public/app.js` has no error handling, so a failed add shows nothing.

Plan: one `back` task covers all seven criteria. The page change is about three lines, so a separate front task would cost more than it saves.
- Add a small title validator in `src/app.ts`. A title must be a string, non-empty after trimming, and at most 200 characters after trimming. The check order is JSON, then required, then length. Titles are saved trimmed.
- POST validates `body.title`. PATCH validates only when the body has a `title` key, so `null` counts as present and gives 400. A PATCH with only `done` still works. Validation runs before any DB call, so nothing is created or changed on failure.
- A body that is `null`, an array or a number is treated as having no title, so POST gives 400 "title is required".
- `readJson` turns a parse failure into a typed 400 error "invalid JSON body", on POST and PATCH.
- The top-level catch answers 400 for these known errors. For anything else it logs the real error with `console.error` and sends 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`.
- In `public/app.js`, the submit handler catches the error and calls the existing `show(err)`. The input keeps its text, and `form.reset()` runs only on success.
- Tests go in `test/tasks.test.ts`, run with `npm test`.

Out of scope: auth, DB constraints or migrations, validating `done` or ids, body size limits, and any change to success responses. No blocking question.

acceptance.text: POST /api/tasks with a missing, empty, whitespace-only or non-string title (or a body that is not an object) answers 400 {"error":"title is required"} and creates no task.
PATCH /api/tasks/:id with a `title` key follows the same rule and leaves the task unchanged on failure; a PATCH without `title` (only `done`) still works.
A title over 200 characters after trimming answers 400 {"error":"title must be at most 200 characters"} on POST and PATCH; exactly 200 is accepted; titles are saved trimmed.
A body that is not valid JSON answers 400 {"error":"invalid JSON body"} on POST and PATCH.
An unexpected error answers 500 {"error":"internal error"} without the internal message; the real error is logged on the server with console.error.
When adding a task fails, the page shows the API's error message in #error and the input keeps its text.
Tests in test/tasks.test.ts cover AC1 to AC5 on POST and PATCH.

out_of_scope: A browser test for the page change

tasks.goal: Fix input validation and error handling. (1) In `src/app.ts`: add a typed client error (e.g. `class HttpError extends Error { status }`) and a title validator. The validator takes `unknown` and returns the trimmed title. It throws 400 'title is required' if the value is not a string or is empty after trim(), then 400 'title must be at most 200 characters' if the trimmed length is over 200 (exactly 200 is OK). In `readJson`, wrap JSON.parse and throw 400 'invalid JSON body' on failure; keep returning {} for an empty body. Treat a parsed body that is null, an array or a non-object as {}, so POST gives 'title is required'. POST /api/tasks: validate `body.title` and call `tasks.createTask(db, trimmedTitle)`. PATCH /api/tasks/:id: validate only when `'title' in body` (so `title: null` gives 400 'title is required'), pass the trimmed title to `updateTask`, and leave a PATCH with only `done` unchanged. Validation must run before any DB call, so a failed request creates or changes nothing. Check order: JSON, then required, then length. Replace the catch in `createServer` (currently `send(res, 500, { error: err.message })`): for HttpError send its status and message; for anything else `console.error(err)` and send 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`. Never send err.message for non-HttpError. Success responses stay as they are (201 on POST, 200 on PATCH, 404 for an unknown id). Keep `src/tasks.ts` as is unless a type needs adjusting. (2) In `public/app.js`: in the submit handler wrap the api call, `form.reset()` and `render()` so a failure calls the existing `show(err)` (e.g. try/catch, or `.then(..., show)` like the other actions). Call `form.reset()` only on success so the input keeps its text on failure. Do not touch the markup: #error is already role=alert. (3) In `test/tasks.test.ts`, using the existing `call` helper (it JSON.stringifies, so for the invalid-JSON case add a raw fetch helper sending a malformed string with content-type application/json), add tests for: POST with {}, {title:''}, {title:'   '}, {title:123}, {title:null}, and body `null` or `[]`, each giving 400 'title is required' with the task count unchanged; POST title of 201 chars giving 400 'title must be at most 200 characters'; 200 chars accepted; ' padded ' saved as 'padded'; a title of 200 chars plus surrounding spaces accepted; PATCH with title '', '  ', 5, null giving 400 'title is required' with the task unchanged; PATCH with a too-long title giving 400; PATCH with a valid title saving it trimmed; PATCH with only {done:true} still 200; invalid JSON on POST and PATCH giving 400 'invalid JSON body'; an unexpected error giving 500 {error:'internal error'} with no internal text, for example by closing/breaking the DB or making a handler throw so the body of the response does not contain the original message (silence or stub console.error in that test). Run `npm test` and make it pass.

reviews.summary:
I found nothing that must change. I read the full diff of `src/app.ts`, `public/app.js` and `test/tasks.test.ts` against the base commit, and ran `npm test`: 26 tests pass, 0 fail.

Checked against the criteria:
- **AC1 and AC2:** `validateTitle` runs before any database call on POST. On PATCH it runs only when `"title" in body`. A missing, empty, blank or non-string title, a `null` title, and a `null` or array body all give 400 "title is required". A PATCH with only `done` is unchanged.
- **AC3:** 200 characters is accepted and 201 is rejected, measured after trimming. Titles are saved trimmed. The check order is required, then length.
- **AC4:** `readJson` turns a parse failure into 400 "invalid JSON body". An empty body still gives `{}`.
- **AC5:** the top-level catch sends an `HttpError`'s own message. Anything else is logged with `console.error` and answers 500 "internal error", so no internal message reaches the client. `HttpError` is declared after its first use, but it only runs at request time, after the module has loaded.
- **AC6:** the submit handler now has try/catch calling `show(err)`. `form.reset()` runs only after a successful add, so the input keeps its text on failure. I did not run the page in a browser, and the ticket puts a browser test out of scope.
- **AC7:** the tests go through the real HTTP server. They check status, body, and that the task count or the task is unchanged. The 500 test breaks the database from a second connection, then checks that "no such table" is absent from the response and that `console.error` was called once. They would fail without the feature, so they have value.

Minor and not worth a finding: an empty request body (as opposed to `{}`) is not tested on POST, though that path is unchanged and gives the same 400 through `{}`.

Not reviewed: security hardening beyond error disclosure, such as body size limits, which are out of scope.

report.summary:
The ticket's 7 criteria are testable, and I adopted them as written. No blocking doubt. I read src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, public/app.js and test/tasks.test.ts.

Findings from the code:
- POST /api/tasks passes body.title straight to SQLite, so a missing or non-string title gives the 500. An empty title is accepted.
- PATCH accepts any title. `changes.title ?? task.title` keeps the old title when none is sent. An empty or non-string title would be saved.
- readJson uses JSON.parse, so bad JSON throws and reaches the catch in createServer. That catch sends err.message with a 500. This is the leak criterion AC5 closes.
- public/app.js: the submit handler awaits api() with no try/catch. The rejection is unhandled, so the page shows nothing. Other actions use `.then(render, show)`. #error is `role=alert`, so reusing show() fits.

Acceptance criteria (source: the ticket):
- AC1: POST with a missing, empty, whitespace-only or non-string title gives 400 `{"error":"title is required"}` and creates no task.
- AC2: PATCH with a `title` key in the body follows the same rule, and the task is unchanged on failure. A PATCH with no `title` (only `done`) still works.
- AC3: A trimmed title over 200 characters gives 400 `{"error":"title must be at most 200 characters"}` on POST and PATCH. Exactly 200 is accepted. Titles are saved trimmed.
- AC4: A body that is not valid JSON gives 400 `{"error":"invalid JSON body"}` on POST and PATCH.
- AC5: Any other unexpected error gives 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`. The real error is logged on the server (console.error).
- AC6: When adding a task fails, the page shows the API's error message in #error. The input keeps its text.
- AC7: Tests in test/tasks.test.ts cover AC1 to AC5 on POST and PATCH. The page change (AC6) needs no browser test.

Decisions: a JSON body that is not an object (`null`, an array, a number) is treated as a missing title, so POST gives 400 "title is required". Check order is JSON, then required, then length. A PATCH whose title is `null` counts as present and gives 400.

Out of scope: auth, a DB-level constraint or migration, validating `done`, ID or filter values, body size limits, any change to the success responses.

affected_views.state: adding a task with an empty title or an API error shows the message in the #error alert

out_of_scope_findings: PATCH `done` is not validated: a string such as "no" is truthy and sets done.
GET /api/tasks?done=false is treated as done (the string "false" is truthy).
readJson has no body size limit.
A JSON body that is an array or null on PATCH would throw on property access, which becomes the generic 500 after AC5.
Non-numeric task ids fall through to a generic 404.

report.summary:
Bad input to the tasks API now answers 400 with a clear message, and unexpected errors answer a generic 500. `npm test` passes: 26 tests, 0 failures, 19 of them new. I did not run the page in a browser, and the ticket puts a browser test out of scope.

**src/app.ts**
- A new `HttpError` (status and message) marks errors that are safe to show the client.
- `validateTitle` takes an unknown value and returns the trimmed title. It throws 400 "title is required" if the value isn't a string or is empty after trimming. It then throws 400 "title must be at most 200 characters" if the trimmed title is over 200. Exactly 200 is accepted.
- `readJson` answers 400 "invalid JSON body" when parsing fails. An empty body still gives `{}`, and a body of `null`, an array or a non-object is also treated as `{}`.
- POST validates the title before any database call and saves the trimmed value.
- PATCH validates only when the body has a `title` key, so `title: null` gives 400. A PATCH with only `done` works as before. Failed requests change nothing.
- The top-level catch sends an `HttpError`'s own status and message. For anything else it calls `console.error(err)` and sends 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`.
- Success responses are unchanged. `src/tasks.ts` is untouched.

**public/app.js:** the submit handler is now in a try/catch that calls the existing `show(err)`. `form.reset()` runs only after a successful add, so the input keeps its text on failure. The markup is untouched.

**test/tasks.test.ts**
- POST: every bad title case from the task, plus bodies `null` and `[]`, each checked for 400 and an unchanged task count. Also a 201-character title, 200 characters accepted (with and without surrounding spaces), and `" padded "` saved as `padded`.
- PATCH: title `''`, `'  '`, `5` and `null` give 400 and leave the task unchanged. A title that is too long gives 400, a valid title is saved trimmed, and a PATCH with only `done` works.
- Invalid JSON on POST and PATCH gives 400.
- The unexpected-error test starts a server on a temporary database file and drops the `tasks` table from a second connection. It checks for 500 "internal error", that "no such table" is absent from the response, and that `console.error` was called once.

Commands run: `npm test` (26 pass, 0 fail).

out_of_scope_findings: PATCH `done` is not validated: any truthy value, such as an object or a string, counts as true.
The `done` filter on GET /api/tasks is not validated: `?done=false` is treated as true because any non-empty string is truthy.
There is no request body size limit.
The page's submit handler does not catch a failure of render() after a successful add separately. It is shown through the same show(), which is acceptable.

report.summary:
No vulnerabilities confirmed in this change. It closes the error-message leak it set out to fix (A10:2025).

I read the diff of src/app.ts and public/app.js against main. I did not run the tests or a dependency audit. The change adds no dependencies, and package.json has none.

What I checked:
- **Error disclosure (A10:2025):** The top-level catch sends the real message only for HttpError, whose messages are fixed strings written in the code. Everything else is logged with console.error and answers a generic 500 "internal error". Before, a 500 with SQLite or JSON-parser text went to any client. This is now closed.
- **Fail-open:** Validation runs before any database call. Bad JSON, a missing title, a title that is not a string, and a body of null or an array all end in a 400 and no write. A PATCH with only `done` skips title validation, as specified.
- **Injection:** The database calls come from src/tasks.ts, which the diff did not touch. Per the task description, the trimmed title reaches it as a value, not as concatenated SQL. The page writes the API's error message with `textContent`, not `innerHTML`, so a message cannot inject markup (no XSS).
- **Input abuse:** The 200-character limit applies after trimming, so the stored title is bounded. `"title" in body` is safe because the parsed body is a plain object. A key like `__proto__` set via JSON.parse is an own property, with no prototype pollution.

What I did not check:
- Authentication and authorization. There are none in the app, and the ticket puts them out of scope.
- Request body size limits. `readJson` still concatenates the whole body into memory, so a large body could exhaust memory (denial of service). This existed before the change.
- Validation of `done`. A non-boolean `done` on PATCH reaches SQLite and now answers a generic 500 rather than a leak. A 400 would be cleaner.
- Security headers, CORS and rate limiting.
out_of_scope_findings: A06:2025 (hardening, not confirmed): readJson in src/app.ts has no body size limit, so a very large request body is buffered in memory. This existed before the change.
The `done` field on PATCH is not validated. A non-boolean value reaches SQLite and now answers a generic 500 (no leak) where a 400 would be cleaner.
The app has no authentication, so anyone who can reach it can read, change and delete every task. The ticket puts this out of scope.
